result.summary: Independently re-verified all seven checks against real source, not the design's self-report. (1) Read the real lib/letflow/engine/transition.ex lines 720-862: gateway_role/2 (730-741), dispatch_parallel_split/4 (748-799), find_matching_join/2 (804-828), walk_to_gateway/3 (830-862) -- design's line numbers and clause structure are accurate. collect_leaf_gateways/3's @spec (Graph.t(), String.t(), MapSet.t(String.t()) -> MapSet.t(branch_leaf())), the branch_leaf type, and the 4-step traversal (cycle check / node lookup / PARALLEL_GATEWAY terminal / out-degree case split) are stated with no open judgment calls left for ELIXIR-DEV -- every branch of the out-degree case (0, 1, >1) has an exact return value spec. (2) Re-derived the nested-PARALLEL_GATEWAY exclusion myself: since step 3's PARALLEL_GATEWAY-terminal check always fires before step 4's broadened out-degree logic can be reached, and a PARALLEL_GATEWAY node's own further edges are never inspected, a nested split's leaf value is always {:gateway, nested_split_id} -- distinct from the branch's real join id in the normal (non-degenerate) case, so the per-branch/cross-branch agreement rule (2.5) rejects it as {:error, :no_matching_join} rather than silently mismatching a JoinCounter cohort. This is the correct, minimal boundary and matches ISSUE-FIXER's own risk framing. The one named residual (a branch that is a bare single-edge chain straight into a nested split with zero other branching) is honestly disclosed as pre-existing, unchanged behavior, not newly introduced. (3) Manually re-traced the diamond example (A -> gw(EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY) -> {B,C} -> D -> join) by hand: with per-path visited sets ({A,gw,B} vs {A,gw,C}), both sibling recursions reach D independently without tripping the cycle guard, union = singleton {{:gateway,"join"}} -- correct. Confirmed that a shared/global visited set would incorrectly have the second sibling find D already visited and wrongly return :dead_end -- the design's justification for per-path (not merged) visited threading holds. (4) Read the real three_branch_graph/0 fixture (parallel_gateway_test.exs lines 50-64) and manually traced AC1 and AC4 through both OLD walk_to_gateway/3 and NEW collect_leaf_gateways/3: each of the 3 split edges targets "join" directly, so both old code (PARALLEL_GATEWAY clause fires immediately, {:ok,"join"}) and new code (step 3 fires immediately, singleton {{:gateway,"join"}}, per-branch check resolves to "join") produce byte-for-byte identical {:ok,"join"} results with zero hops -- step 4's broadened out-degree logic is never reached for this fixture, confirming the design's 'dead code for all existing tests' claim is genuinely true, not just asserted. AC1's JoinCounter/branch_ids assertions and AC4's all-cancelled path both depend only on this same find_matching_join/2 return value plus unchanged downstream dispatch_parallel_join/4 logic, so both are unaffected. (5) Read the new test specs (section 4): branch_with_exclusive_gateway_graph/0 genuinely exercises the new out-degree>1 union-of-siblings path (an EXCLUSIVE_GATEWAY with 2 edges reconverging on the join, the exact ISS-0398/kyc-routing shape) with a meaningful positive assertion (split now succeeds, correct JoinCounter, correct token placement on "gw"). ambiguous_branch_dead_ends_graph/0 genuinely exercises the per-branch singleton-rejection rule with a mixed dead-end/gateway leaf set, asserting the fix still correctly errors on genuine ambiguity -- neither spec is vacuous. (6) Read lib/letflow/design/req051-parallel-gateway-split-join.md sections 3.3 (lines 261-282) and 12.4 (lines 631-639) directly -- the design's quotations of both sections are verbatim-accurate, and its characterization (a named, never-closed OQ, not a hidden bug) is correctly grounded. Independently re-ran the design's own claimed grep (grep -rli 'nested.*parallel|block-structured|internal.*branch' docs/issues/*.yaml) -- zero hits, confirming no existing issue covers the nested-PARALLEL_GATEWAY-within-a-branch case, so the follow-up-issue recommendation in section 6 is warranted and not a duplicate. (7) Scanned the entire design document for defmodule/defstruct/def/defp -- zero hits (only bare @spec/@type declarations and prose/worked-example traces), confirming no implementation code is present. All seven checks hold under independent re-derivation. No defects found; the design is unambiguous enough for ELIXIR-DEV to implement without further judgment calls.
